sections.title: Executive verdict
sections.text:
Acme India is a railway interiors, refurbishment and component-supply contractor with real execution history and a substantial order book, but cash realization and financial stewardship are material weaknesses. FY 2026 consolidated revenue was ₹263.7077 crore and owner PAT ₹24.3577 crore; CFO was negative ₹11.5016 crore before financing-classified interest. Receivables reached ₹252.1846 crore, including ₹79.3897 crore due from one newly significant related-party customer. The IPO provides capital, not proof of collection or resolution of old dues. Classification: Avoid — governance under the framework’s evidenced GOV 3 override, with a separate unresolved funding/collection hold. This is not an allegation of fraud, a conviction, or a finding of current insolvency. BQS is capped at 3, Growth Quality is 5.00, and IAS remains NS.

Model correction dated20 October2026: opening obligations and terminal claims have been reconciled separately from new forecast expenses. Reported historical financial statements are unchanged. The corrected scenario values are in section10.

sections.title: Research header, scope, identity and gates
sections.text: Acme India Industries Limited, BSE SME 544981, symbol ACMERAIL, ISIN INE162701010; listed 9 October 2026. Cutoff 20 October 2026, five-year assessment horizon and 15% nominal equity hurdle before investor taxes. Accounts use Indian GAAP Accounting Standards under Section 133, not Ind AS. Consolidated FY 2024–2026 accounts include changing controlled subsidiaries; original FY 2023 is standalone. Secondary quote ₹216.55 dated 19 October 15:28 IST ×2.34722 crore post-IPO shares gives ₹508.2905 crore, not the stale ₹534.93 crore market capitalization on the same page. No official BSE close was independently obtained. Historical evidence confidence Medium, current funding/collections Low. G 1 conditional with sufficient adverse stewardship evidence for GOV 3; G 2 hold for material reconciliation/collection questions; G 3 hold, not proven default; G 4 unverified because only seven listed sessions and no complete post-listing turnover/restriction history.

sections.title: Scorecard and audit
sections.text: Canonical factors: GOV 3, MOAT 5, REV 6, DUR 6, CAP 3, CASH 2, BAL 4, EXEC 5, EARN 5. BQS raw 4.20 is capped at 3 by GOV≤3; final Q 3 is carried into IAS without alteration. Growth Quality raw 5.00 equals the persistent weak-cash cap 5. IAS R and L are NS; D 2 and P 3 are supported adverse judgments. Known IAS weighted sum 1.45 at 55% coverage gives raw missing-data bounds 1.90–5.95 before the governance cap; the cap does not convert an incomplete score into a numeric IAS. All investable-ranking eligibility is false. Forecast uncertainties are not silently filled with optimistic scores.

sections.title: Business economics and competitive position
sections.text: The company designs, manufactures, installs and provides warranty maintenance for railway coach interiors, with tender-based turnkey furnishing, refurbishment, toilet upgrades and component supply. Its predecessor began in 2012; company incorporation was December 2021 and the takeover agreement valuation was January 2022. Claimed completed 1,610 new-coach furnishing,1,888 refurbishment and 10,948 toilet units include predecessor work. Railway approvals, installed experience and local execution relationships are useful qualification advantages, but price competition, customer concentration and working-capital demands constrain excess returns. The Sonipat facility is about 92,000 square feet; utilization measures compare actual single-shift output with 24-hour capacity, so apparent spare capacity is not a free growth forecast. FY 2026 contract/service mix shifted dramatically: turnkey fell from₹108.3340 to₹21.8172 crore, electrical/other supplies rose from₹32.3851 to₹140.0681 crore, toilets₹57.9886 and refurbishment₹24.7717. Trading/supply growth should not be valued as recurring software or subscription income.

sections.title: Industry runway, order book and concentration
sections.text: June 30 order book was₹737.9733 crore across 40 orders, about 2.8 times FY 2026 sales: toilet upgrades 46.92%, private-client supply 31.04%, refurbishment 9.13%, turnkey 8.51% and direct rail supply 4.40%. The auditor certificate and contract disclosure support the backlog figure, not guaranteed timing, margins or collection. Direct Indian Railways sales dropped to 46.77% from 91.54%, but related/private intermediaries remain exposed to the same rail ecosystem; this is not automatically customer-risk diversification. Top-ten supplier concentration rose to 76.95% from 66.88% and 58.15%; no long-term supplier contracts were evidenced. Repair orders and CCTV/voice-recording product plans provide accessible optionality, but issuer-commissioned industry TAM is not company revenue. H 2 accounted for 91.13% of FY 2026 sales, so neither small H 1 nor a single strong March period is safely annualized.

sections.title: Governance, ownership and minority treatment
sections.text: Post-listing promoter ownership is 64.46% across Suraj and Sadhvi Pandey; public 35.54% comprises 2,353 holders. All promoter shares and 46.74% of public shares were locked atOctober 9, together 81.07% of total equity. No encumbrances, warrants, convertibles or ESOP dilution were disclosed in that filing. These are dated facts, not permanent free-float assumptions. FY 2026 promoter-director remuneration₹4.8 crore was about 19.7% of owner PAT, versus₹3.78 crore FY 2025 and₹0.72 crore FY 2024. Stewardship concerns are specific: personal assets₹18.2472 crore and unidentified liabilities₹35.4361 crore from the predecessor takeover were reversed to the promoter through the director-loan account; creditor exposure is not extinguished merely by promoter indemnity. Repeated bank-statement discrepancies, significant statutory-payment delays, related-party collection exposure and subsidiary audit-trail failures justify GOV 3. Contrary evidence includes substantial promoter ownership, disclosure of these matters and an unmodified audit opinion; these do not cure the observed weaknesses. No claim of intentional diversion is made.

sections.title: Financial history and normalization
sections.text: Consolidated FY 2024/FY 2025/FY 2026 revenue was₹213.4346/209.9952/263.7077 crore; group PAT₹19.2072/16.4003/24.3320 and owner PAT₹19.2072/16.4568/24.3577. Minority losses increase owner profit, not decrease it. Original FY 2023 standalone revenue₹140.9139 crore and PAT₹8.0507 are contextual, not blindly spliced into the changing consolidated series. FY 2024–2026 revenue CAGR 11.15% supports REV 6 with no trajectory uplift; The older restatement instead reports FY 2023 standalone revenue 137.1873 and PAT 7.5645, versus original 140.9139 and 8.0507; three-year mixed-scope growth is 24.35%, not a verified organic CAGR. The original/restated revenue difference is not silently erased. Restatement raised original FY 2024 owner PAT 18.8822 to 19.2073 and FY 2025 from 15.7975 to 16.4568 through tax, MSME interest, depreciation and employee-benefit adjustments. FY 2026 PBT 33.2205 includes other income 4.1795 and liquidated-damage recovery.5596. Removing both with 25–30% tax gives owner PAT roughly 19.9627–21.3868 crore, versus reported 24.3577. At full post-IPO shares this is EPS₹8.50–9.11, not the weighted pre-IPO reported₹14.10. Published EBITDA 39.8159 adds interest but retains other finance charges; adding the entire finance-cost line would overstate that definition.

sections.title: Cash conversion and working-capital forensics
sections.text: FY 2024/FY 2025/FY 2026 CFO was−₹6.0937/+₹23.9728/−₹11.5016 crore, just₹6.3775 crore cumulatively against₹59.9395 crore group PAT, or 10.64%. Cash interest classified under financing was₹5.2918/9.7566/12.3948 crore, making cash after interest substantially worse. FY 2026 CFO absorbed₹94.1124 crore receivables,₹10.2292 crore inventory and₹3.6458 crore other current assets, partly financed by₹46.7821 crore additional payables and₹6.2477 crore other liabilities. Receivables₹252.1846 crore include₹37.2281 crore unbilled amounts; do not add them twice. Gross aged receivables over one year were₹26.4989 crore with only₹0.1163 crore total allowance. Inventory₹40.2341, supplier advances₹7.6499 and payables₹162.7683 imply actual core WC₹137.3003 crore. Earlier FY 2023 restated standalone CFO was−9.6464, financing interest 2.3425 and cash capex 2.6748, reinforcing the cash concern without pretending the perimeter is identical. Cash capex₹1.1621/1.9862/.6286 does not make this asset-light cash generation: FDs, security deposits and customer credit consume capital. FY 2026 unpaid income-tax provision 14.8717, TDS 2.9534, GST 5.1792 and MSME-interest payable 3.2823 are obligations, not free funding forever.

sections.title: Accounting, related parties and legal risk
sections.text: Vibhata Solutions LLP FY 2026 related-party sales₹67.2794 crore and receivable₹79.3897 crore are almost exactly linked by 18% GST, consistent with substantial uncollected gross billing; ledger confirmation is needed, not a fraud conclusion. Vibgyor Innovations sales₹30.6445 crore add to external related sales of about 37.1% of group revenue; disclosed sales to controlled subsidiaries are not added again after consolidation. Long-term related loans₹2.7040 crore and other related advances require recovery checks. Auditor KAM addresses year-end revenue recognition against delivery/inspection. FY 2026 subsidiary audit trails did not operate throughout the year, contrary to the generic Tally note; FY 2025 trails also were not enabled/preserved fully. FY 2025 March bank-reported receivables 84.8421 versus unaudited books 182.2247, and FY 2026 security-deposit reporting 40.1296 versus 3.8353, are parent-scope discrepancies, not consolidated numbers. Management explanations do not constitute an independently reconciled cash trail. The signed audit opinion is unmodified, with other-auditor reliance and an unconsolidated inactive partnership whose accounts were unavailable. Pending stopped-cheque, software-license and tax disputes are contested, not convictions. The October 16 Schneider hearing outcome was not established by cutoff.

sections.title: Capital allocation, reinvestment and financing
sections.text:
Invested-capital proxy equity plus debt less free cash rose₹105.2160→136.1561→188.3830 crore; pledged FDs remain employed capital. Conservative operating EBIT retains statutory/MSME interest and other finance charges, adding back only bank/other borrowing interest:₹25.3109/25.9558/34.8336. At 25% tax, incremental NOPAT/added capital is 1.56% FY 2025,12.75% FY 2026 and 8.59% across two years, below an analyst 12–16% capital-cost range overall; this is timing-sensitive, not a project IRR. FY 2026 total finance cost 12.7123 includes borrowing interest 6.3522, MSME interest 1.2249, statutory-dues interest 2.2310 and other charges 2.9042. IPO repayment cannot simply remove all of it. Fresh issue 54.072 lakh shares at₹196 raises₹105.9811 crore gross, but net proceeds are₹86.7307 crore after stated issuer costs; OFS₹15.7114 crore is not company cash. Pre-IPO₹20.52 crore at₹190 was already raised in December 2025 and is already inside March balances. Objects: debt 41, WC 38, capex 6.273 and GCP 1.4577 crore. Actual October deployment/collections remain unverified.

Model correction, 20 October 2026: this changes our cash-flow/terminal-claim treatment, not the issuer’s reported history. The original model already paid ₹26.8257 crore identified opening tax/statutory/MSME-interest/CSR claims once. Add excluded accrued borrowing interest ₹0.2346 crore and current employee provision ₹0.0275 crore, using the printed subtotal: additional ₹0.2621 crore. The ₹0.0001 crore difference between provision components and subtotal is rounding, not an invented liability. sections.title: Balance-sheet resilience and contingent obligations
sections.text: March 2026 debt₹85.1821 crore and free cash₹0.3462 contrast with current/noncurrent pledged FDs₹35.4460/8.5208 crore. Do not net those deposits as immediately available cash. Total disclosed contingencies₹94.6366 crore reconcile to guarantees 44.0256, LCs 29.8761, tax/TDS 14.6915, claims 3.3637 and ITAT 2.6798; the introductory risk paragraph has a different total, so the component table controls. Guarantee/LC face amounts are not all incremental cash debt or independent of underlying suppliers. Some undisputed FY 2025 tax and TDS arrears were paid by the audit-report date, but FY 2026 advance-tax arrears₹3.0931 crore remained unpaid in that disclosure. A conditional IPO bridge lowers gross debt to 44.1821 and raises cash to 46.0769 before other uses, not an observed October balance sheet. The company projects parent payables falling from 154.8172 to 76.7448 crore while receivables decline from 263.0935 to 220.1513: supplier normalization can consume more cash than debtor release provides. Refinancing, timely collection and earmarked-cash discipline remain material.

sections.title: Valuation, peer boundaries and linked scenarios
sections.text: At secondary₹216.55, equity value₹508.2905 crore is 20.87 times reported owner PAT and about 23.77–25.46 times normalized PAT; post-IPO shares are used consistently. The prospectus states no directly comparable listed company. Railway rolling-stock OEMs, outsourced contractors and interior-component suppliers differ materially, so no invented peer median is used. The attached annual model starts from actual March core WC 137.3003, adds net IPO once, repays 41, excludes pledged FDs, settles 27.0878 legacy tax, interest and current employee claims, funds 6.273 capex and an explicit 11.554 additional-FD sensitivity. Base growth 15/12/10/8/8%, EBIT margin 13%,30 debtor release and 50 payable normalization produces a₹12.8283 crore peak funding gap; no valid base IRR is assigned. Bull 25/20/15/12/10%,15% margin and 60 debtor release stays funded and yields 12.69% five-year IRR at 10 x terminal EBITDA, below 15% hurdle. Bear revenue−25% then 0/5/5/5%,8% margin,60 extra collection days,75 payable normalization, capped non-overlapping debtor haircut, inventory loss and 10 claims creates₹138.3046 crore gap without assumed rescue. These are linked stress assumptions, not predictions or current defaults. R remains NS because actual post-IPO collections/deployment and financing are material; sensitivities and unsupported-return illustrations are kept separate.

sections.title: Ownership, trading liquidity and implementation
sections.text: Official security data corroborate 2.34722 crore shares and 600-share board lot, costing₹129,930 at the dated secondary quote. Only seven potential trading sessions existed between October 9 listing and October 19; pre-listing days must never be filled as zero-volume days. One secondary observed session had 118,800 traded shares, but a single day or rounded five-day chart cannot supply the required 20/60-session lower mean/median test. Current BSE ASM/GSM/other restrictions, live spread and executable depth were not independently established. L and₹5-lakh practical-exit-day estimate therefore remain NS. The same quote page’s bands appear updated separately from its last trade, so they are not asserted as the 19 October band. High lock-in and market-maker designation do not guarantee two-way liquidity. Recovered dated secondary history corroborates the October 19 quote and contains 6 post-listing rows, fewer than a complete 20/60-session series. Observed lower-turnover median is ₹54415425 per day, giving a purely illustrative ₹5 lakh / 5% participation exit of 0.18 observed sessions. Low/high times volume are turnover bounds, not reported turnover. The short IPO record, missing listing-session row and unverified BSE restrictions keep L NS; pre-listing dates remain excluded.

sections.title: Bear case, falsification and monitoring
sections.text: The decisive variable is collection of billed and unbilled receivables while suppliers and statutory creditors are paid. A railway spending headline or new order does not invalidate the bear case without cash. Review: (1) Vibhata gross 79.3897 receivable with matching ledger/GST and subsequent receipts; absence of receipts after contractual milestones is an investigation trigger. (2) AR 252.1846 and >one-year 26.4989, with ageing migration and adequate provisioning. (3) Supplier 162.7683 and tax/dues settlement, reconciled to bank cash rather than another liability increase. (4) IPO net 86.7307 actual deployment, including debt 41 and expense/prepayment reconciliation. (5) Bank submission differences and all-subsidiary audit trails corrected and independently tested. (6) Order 737.9733 conversion to inspected delivery and cash, not only sales. (7) Income-tax and Schneider/Siemens proceedings, distinguishing allegations from adjudicated outcomes. (8) Complete post-listing turnover, restrictions and lock-in expiry. Improvement requires corroborated cash and controls over at least a reporting cycle; another material unreconciled related-party transaction or funding breach would worsen the classification.

sections.title: Final synthesis, multibagger feasibility and open evidence
sections.text: A real rail-industry position and backlog are the strongest positive counterarguments, and fresh capital can reduce expensive borrowing. They do not erase weak accumulated cash conversion, recurring overdue costs, control exceptions or concentrated related-party balances. A 5 x/10 x claim is unsupported: at unchanged share count and valuation it requires corresponding growth in sustainable owner earnings, while lower exit multiples require still more; neither order-book face value nor promoter lock-in proves that outcome. Historical factors can be scored conservatively, but the current cash/debt/collection bridge and short trading record prevent complete IAS. The dossier is a completed deep assessment with explicit unresolved evidence, not a completed investment recommendation or a screen pretending to be deep. Next evidence: post-IPO bank/monitoring deployment, subsequent collections, current restricted-cash status, corrected audit/bank reconciliations, and exchange trading/restriction data.

valuation.assumptions: Actual opening core WC, never back-calculated from forecast ratios. Pledged FDs not free cash; additional11.554 reflects issuer projected current FD47 versus35.446, not a verified bank demand. Net IPO already subtracts all issue costs; eligible opening IPO prepayments1.8861 may increase cash, shown as separate sensitivity to avoid hidden double-charge. March tax provision14.8717, TDS2.9534, GST5.1792, PF.0089, MSME interest3.2823, statutory interest.2308 and CSR.2994 settled once; no double inclusion in core WC. Future tax25% cash, costs of ordinary nonbank/statutory/MSME charges retained within EBIT margin; borrowing interest11% base/bull and14% bear. Other opening operating assets/liabilities held flat, no assumed release of tax advances or related loans. Delta core WC40% incremental sales, plus explicit collection/payable normalization. Bear allows no contraction release,60 extra collection days and separately stated AR/inventory stress; use the larger of 25% of Vibhata AR or 25% of aged AR rather than adding potentially overlapping balances; this is a conservative stress, not an observed loss. Existing debt rolled except.1 annual principal, no new rescue debt/equity or dividends. Terminal EV/EBITDA multiples8/10/5 are analyst sensitivities, not verified peer targets. Reserve3 deducted once at exit.

model_correction_2026_10_20.classification: Ordinary salary, audit and operating expense payable stocks remain in opening and forecast closing operating WC in the reference case. Net incremental WC assumptions include like-for-like replacement accruals; accelerated-stock sensitivity pays these additional balances once. This does not assert permanent nonpayment of individual invoices.
model_correction_2026_10_20.terminal_policy: Opening noncurrent employee/deposit claim retained at terminal, not assumed immediately due. Future operating margins include new employee costs; no extra growth in old provision or asset recovery is credited.
model_correction_2026_10_20.tax_policy: Net-tax credits excluded from opening WC/financial-asset recovery. No-credit sensitivity tests usability; unknown Adisoft government-credit composition is explicitly conditional.
model_correction_2026_10_20.attribution: Correction to analyst model, not an issuer financial restatement or new allegation.
model_correction_2026_10_20.ordinary_stock_policy: The identified ordinary operating payable stock is held constant in nominal rupees in the reference opening and every forecast closing balance. Individual invoices are paid and replaced by like-for-like accruals. No extra cash is generated from growing that stock. The stated incremental WC forecast is after this constant stock; accelerated-settlement sensitivity reduces the stock to zero once and never charges it again.
